test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following components in the axle is the most likely to fail if there is an unusual loud clanking or clunking as you put your vehicle into gear, or if a vehicle seems to struggle to get power as it starts to move?

options.text: There is a crack initiated in the axle at cross sectional area perpendicular to axis
Bearing at the wheel is damaged

solution:
The correct answer is __Axle-joint damage**(Option 3)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Axle-joint damage__ can cause unusual loud clanking or clunking noises when putting the vehicle into gear.
 
• It can also result in the vehicle struggling to gain power as it starts to move.
 
• The axle joints, including CV joints, are crucial for the smooth transfer of power from the transmission to the wheels.
 
• Damage or wear in these joints can lead to poor performance and audible noises.
 
• Regular maintenance and inspections can help identify and rectify such issues early.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Bending in the shaft induced:**

 
 
• This occurs due to excessive loads or impacts but typically does not cause clanking noises.
 
 
 
• **Crack initiated in the axle:**
 
 
• Cracks can compromise the axle's integrity, leading to eventual failure, but loud noises are usually not the first symptom.
 
 
 
• **Bearing at the wheel is damaged:**
 
 
• Damaged wheel bearings typically cause grinding or humming noises rather than clanking.
